 Follow “Forrest Gump” star Gary Sinise details son Mac’s final moments before death at 33: ‘Hard to wrap my head around’
 The actor’s book “Graceful Warrior” hit shelves on Nov. 10.
 Shelby Stivale Tue, November 10, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Gary Sinise; Mac Sinise
Credit: Steve Granitz/WireImage; Gary Sinise/Instagram Key Points
 Gary Sinise recalled son Mac's final moments prior to his January 2024 death at 33.
 The Forrest Gump actor's son went through a four-and-a-half year battle with cancer after being diagnosed with a rare bone tumor.
 "I loved him so much," Sinise wrote.
 Forrest Gump alum Gary Sinise recalled son Mac Sinise's final moments in new book Graceful Warrior .
 Sinise shared that Mac lost the ability to breathe in the early hours of Jan. 5, 2024. "The machine was breathing for him now," the actor wrote in the book, published on Tuesday. Sinise watched his son, who had undergone a years-long battle with cancer, and was "feeling a new kind of weight and sadness I hadn't felt before."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Mac was diagnosed with Chordoma, a rare bone tumor, after years of persistent pain from a tailbone injury. He went through an almost five-year battle with cancer prior to his death at age 33 in January 2024 .
 "I was so proud of Mac. I loved him so much. He had fought so hard, and I had fought with him, never letting thoughts of defeat creep in," Sinise wrote. "Yet I could see that, despite all our efforts over the past few days, he would not return to the place where he could simply use a cannula to breathe."
 By 7:00 a.m. that same day, Sinise started calling family members to come to the hospital. (Sinise and wife Moira are parents to Mac, Sophie, 37, and Ella, 34.)
 "Already I felt completely worn out, but I knew I needed to walk my family through this difficult and sacred day," Sinise shared. "After everyone arrived, I took them into the private room and tried to tell them as best I could what the night and early morning had been like. It was tough for me, seeing all their faces."
 Advertisement Advertisement As the morning progressed, a priest came into Mac's hospital room and "delivered last rites." Sinise admitted that "it was hard to wrap my head around that this was happening" as he continued to recount the heartbreaking day.
 "We surrounded Mac with love. Holding hands. Tears in our eyes. A Rosary was said for a bit. His mask was off now. We could see his face," he continued. "Everyone with us. Family. By now, the doctors said Mac could no longer hear us, but I am sure he knew we were there. He was peaceful."
 'Graceful Warrior' by Gary Sinise 
 Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter . 
 Mac died at 3:25 p.m. that day "with the family all around him," the Oscar nominee wrote. Following Mac's death, Sinise "stood with him for a long while, not moving, not speaking." He added, "The feeling I had just then was unlike anything I had ever known, something beyond words, something that can never be fully described. It didn't seem real."
 Advertisement Advertisement Sinise said he could "still feel" Mac's "personality, his winsomeness, his resilience, his grace, his courage, his faith, and the strength that had carried him through," even though he was gone.
 "I could hear his voice, as if he were still talking to me," he wrote. "Mac and I stayed like that for a time, me just staring at him, studying him, remembering him."
 Graceful Warrior: The True Story of a Son, a Father, and a Family Who Carried Each Other Through is out now.
